units.translation: Thus Hermann for ἐπι δρομω [upon the course] (ο written over ω in M) πόθι [where] (with the accent over ο deleted). It is a poetic form for ὅπου [where], not read elsewhere in the tragedians. ὁππόθι [wherever] the later epic poets sometimes said.
where death is absent from the course (ἐπῇ [is present] Weilius).

it is a particle, either adverb or conjunction.
(adverb) how, in what way, as, related to the correlative οὕτως [thus], either expressed or implied, frequent in indirect questions.
οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅπως [there is no way] there is no way, i.e. by no means.
ὅπως [how] related to the preceding πῶς [how].
ὅπως [as] in comparison
ὅπως [how] with a superlative, than.
ὅπως [when] in a temporal sense, when, as.
ὅπως [so that] a conjunction having the meaning of purpose, that. It is constructed with the indicative, subjunctive, and optative, according to the rules common to all final particles.
ὅπως ἂν [so that] with the optative
which is said for metrical reasons instead of ὅπως κυρεῖ [as it happens].
With aposiopesis
where, instead of οὐκ ἔχω [I cannot], which should have followed, the form of the sentence is changed and σαίνομαι δ᾽ ὑπ᾿ ἐλπίδος [I am flattered by hope] is introduced.
Thus Valckenaer for ἢ πῶς [or how].
I wrote for ἀτιμαστῆρα τώς [dishonorer thus].

Corrupt, where the scholiast has ὡς ἔχετε τάχους ποδῶν [as you have speed of feet]. The usage of speech requires ὅπως τάχος [as quickly as possible], with the gloss ποδῶν [of feet] deleted, as Heimsoeth pointed out.
Thus ὅσον τάχιστα [as quickly as possible] ibid. 883.
